post.title: Why online banks can pay 10x the average savings rate
post.ig:
$10,000 in savings: $37 a year, or $400?

FDIC national average savings rate: 0.37% (Sept 21, 2026).
Top online savings accounts: over 4% in late Sept 2026 (Bankrate, Fortune). Rates are variable.
How: no branches. Ally Bank held $144B in retail deposits at the end of 2025 with no branch network, and earned a 3.47% net interest margin.

Sources: FDIC, Bankrate, Fortune, Ally 2025 10-K.
News and education, not financial advice.

post.yt_desc:
The FDIC's national average savings rate was 0.37% in September 2026, while top online savings accounts paid over 4%. On $10,000, that's $37 versus about $400 a year. Online banks like Ally skip branches, use higher rates to gather deposits (Ally held $144 billion at the end of 2025) and lend them out, earning a 3.47% net interest margin. Sources: FDIC, Bankrate, Fortune, Ally 2025 10-K.

News and education, not financial advice.
